notes: Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for mission-critical telemetry inference (anomaly detection, operator chat). Primary ask: predictable throughput with hard latency SLOs and reserved GPU economics.

Workload profile (provided by customer): baseline QPS ~ 12 mixed requests/sec; steady-state token/sec ~ 9k-12k (avg 512 token responses); peak bursts up to 60 QPS during incident windows (short spikes ~ 3-7 minutes).
Latency targets: p95 < 200ms for short prompts (<256 tokens), p95 < 500ms for 512-1024 token responses; objective to keep p99 below 2s under peak with fallback policy.
Throughput guarantee ask: committed baseline 12 QPS with bursting allowance to 60 QPS for up to 10 minutes/hr; want clear billing model for sustained vs burst usage.

Reserved capacity planning: customer prefers a proposal expressed in "A100-equivalent GPU" units. SE note: recommend initial reserved pool = 6 A100-80GB equiv for steady-state with 2 additional burst nodes (H100 option discussed). Provide cost delta for quantized LLMs.

Batching / caching: heavy prefix reuse between field-device diagnostics - opportunity for KV cache + prefix caching to reduce token/sec by ~25%. Ask for Redwood Optimize recommendations and suggested batch windows that preserve p95 latency.

SLA negotiation items: uptime SLA + latency SLO credits, explicit fallback routing (hosted fallback) terms, and RTO for patching windows. Legal wants explicit data residency and audit log retention terms.
Security: require SSO/SAML, KMS integration for key rollovers, and 7-year audit log retention on request (may be a separate add-on).

POC plan: 2-week POC -> measure p50/p95/p99 across steady vs synthetic peak; step 1 (week1): replicate baseline 12 QPS with production prompts; step 2 (week2): synthetic 60 QPS spikes for 5-10 minute windows and observe tail latencies and queueing behavior.
Success criteria for POC: p95 within targets, <20% token cost delta vs baseline forecast, automated fallback triggers functional, and runbook for scale-up validated.
Quotes from customer: 'We need guarantees — not just numbers in a slide. If you're taking our reserved dollars we need defined latency credits and a clear escalation path.'

Operational concerns: their SRE wants control-plane visibility (per-request tracing, token-level cost) and ability to pin model versions during rollouts; asked about canary scaling and automatic rollback policies.

Next deliverables: Redwood to send dedicated sizing spreadsheet (baseline throughput -> GPU count estimate), draft SLA term sheet, POC test harness repo link, and suggested quantization families to evaluate.
Drive artifacts referenced: Redwood sizing deck v2, sample SLA term sheet (template), POC harness README (link provided).

Internal AE/SE notes: prioritize generating two proposals: (A) conservative steady-state focused (6 A100 equiv + burst pool), (B) aggressive latency-first (8 H100 equiv with stricter SLO credits). Include monthly committed vs overage pricing scenarios.
Risks: cross-region residency could force additional reserved pools in EU - increases baseline ARR; legal timeline could push procurement to Q3.
